title: Chemistry — The periodic table
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for KS3 Science (chemistry) (status of the source: authored-reviewed-reverified-2026-10-08). Terms and clues: C6#c01 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; C6.1#xt2 term and clue written for the game; C6#c05 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; C6.1#xt1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: C6#q01, C6#q04, C6#q02, C6#q06, C6#x01 (written for the game), C6#q07.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Element
items.clue: A substance made of only one type of atom.

items.label: Density
items.clue: The mass of a substance in each unit of its volume

items.label: Melting point
items.clue: The temperature at which a solid turns into a liquid.

items.label: Reactivity
items.clue: How readily a substance takes part in chemical changes

questions.stem: Which of these shows a chemical property of an element?

options.text: Gallium melting in a person's hand
Iodine crystals dissolving in ethanol
Magnesium burning brightly in air
Iron and sulfur stirred together

questions.explanation: Yes. Burning makes a new substance, magnesium oxide, so it shows how magnesium reacts: a chemical property.

questions.stem: How did Mendeleev put the elements in order in his table?

options.text: By atomic mass, keeping similar elements together
By atomic number, as today's table does
By atomic mass alone, with no swaps made
By reactivity, from most to least reactive

questions.explanation: Yes. Mendeleev used atomic mass for the order, but put elements with similar properties in the same group, even if that meant swapping a pair.

questions.stem: Chlorine is a gas, bromine a liquid and iodine a solid at room temperature. All three are in Group 7. What does this show?

options.text: These three cannot really all be in one group
Their single atoms are a gas, a liquid and a solid
Only chlorine, as a gas, is a true non-metal
Elements in one group can be in different states

questions.explanation: Yes. Elements in a group react in similar ways, but their physical properties change going down the group: here from gas to liquid to solid.

questions.stem: Mendeleev left a gap in the group with silicon and tin. What did he expect the missing element to be like?

options.text: Like the elements on either side in its row
Similar to silicon and tin in its group
Identical to silicon and tin in every way
Nothing could be said until it was found

questions.explanation: Yes. Elements in a group have similar properties, so he predicted an element like silicon and tin. Germanium, found in 1886, matched his predictions closely.

questions.stem: Sodium and gold are both metals. Sodium reacts violently with water, but gold does not react with it. What does this show?

options.text: Gold cannot be a metal, as metals react
Elements can differ in chemical properties
Sodium must be a non-metal, as it reacts
Their physical properties differ, not chemical

questions.explanation: Reacting with water is a chemical property, and it varies from one element to another.

questions.stem: Argon, the first noble gas to be collected, was found in 1894. Where were the noble gases in Mendeleev's first table, made in 1869?

options.text: In Group 0, just as in today's table
In the gaps he had left for them
At the end, as the least reactive
Nowhere: his table had no place for them

questions.explanation: Yes. Mendeleev did not know a whole group was missing, so his first table had no place for the noble gases. A new group, Group 0, was added later.
